title: Chikoos (Sapota): modeled ₹1,262/qtl left, Barara → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: January 2023: reported chikoos (Sapota) prices at Barara and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 13 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹1,262 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 72 same-variety market pairs screened for chikoos (Sapota) in January 2023; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2023
scenes.caption: Barara (Haryana) and Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported chikoos (Sapota) prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) on 13 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Barara reported a median ₹4,250 per quintal. Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹5,500 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,300/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,300 per quintal, and Kangra (Baijnath) was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 289 km by road
scenes.caption: 289 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹62/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹732 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹439 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kangra (Baijnath) report, the rule selects 13 of 13 modeled shipping days. 13 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹1,262 per quintal (₹967 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Chikoos (Sapota) route from Barara to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 100% of matched days in January 2023. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹126,200, or ₹96,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to chikoos (Sapota)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹62/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Chikoos (Sapota) route from Barara to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 100% of matched days in January 2023. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹126,200, or ₹96,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato
